Consider the curve $\operatorname{ln}⁡x+y=0.$ Given that $x=x(t),\text{ }y=y(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=5$ on the curve at the point $(1,0),$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.

feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{x}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=5,$ $x=1,$ and $y=0,$ and solving for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{x}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 5\cdot \frac{1}{1}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 5+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$
